article_sentences: The hearing on Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s plea to reject an election petition filed against his victory from the Perambur constituency took an interesting turn on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), with Justice V. Lakshminarayanan of the Madras High Court remarking that the entire texture of the case had changed in view of the Supreme Court judgments cited by counsel for the election petitioner.

After hearing the arguments made on behalf of the Chief Minister on Monday and Tuesday, the Judge began firing a volley of questions at the election petitioner’s counsel on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), asking how some alleged discrepancies in assets worth over ₹600 crore declared by Mr. Vijay would amount to undue influence over voters or could be termed as a corrupt electoral practice.

The Judge wanted to know whether the voters in the Perambur constituency would have been swayed in one direction or the other simply because there was a difference of a few crores or a few lakhs in the assets declared by the Chief Minister, especially in light of the fact that he was a “superstar” in the cinema industry and had voluntarily declared both movable and immovable properties worth more than ₹600 crore.
The Judge said he had relied on a chartered accountant to declare his assets while being elevated to the position of a Judge of the High Court.

Therefore, if Mr. Vijay had also declared his assets through a chartered accountant, how could his election itself be declared null and void for any mistakes made by the auditor in such a declaration, the Judge wondered.

He also questioned the challenge made by a voter, S. Dinesh, through his counsel on record, V.R. Shanmuganathan, to the election of the Chief Minister from Perambur on the ground of improper acceptance of the nomination form by the Returning Officer concerned.
The Judge wanted to know how the Returning Officer could be expected to verify the correctness of the declared assets.

In answering the questions, the election petitioner’s counsel said that the Returning Officer was expected to conduct only a summary inquiry, whereas the charge of false declaration, and whether such declaration was made wilfully and deliberately, could be inquired into only by means of leading evidence during the course of trial in an election petition.
Hence, the election petition should not be rejected at the threshold, he argued.

He said, Justice V. Ramasubramanian (during his stint in the Madras High Court before his retirement as a Supreme Court Judge) had in Krishnamoorthy versus Sivakumar (2009) held that “any incorrect information, wrong information, incomplete information, false information, one-sided information, disinformation, misinformation and non-information would certainly interfere with the free exercise of the electoral right of the voter, inasmuch as his choice of candidate will be influenced greatly by the information so furnished or withheld.”
“The view taken by Justice Ramasubramanian was affirmed by the Supreme Court in 2015.
Therefore, I have made out a cause of action for the trial of the election petition and it should not be rejected in limine,” the counsel said.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 7) has held that an election petition filed under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (RP Act) must be presented by the election petitioner himself, and that non-compliance with this mandatory requirement renders the petition liable to be dismissed.

A Bench of Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar upheld the Madras High Court's dismissal of an election petition challenging the election of DMK MLA S. Regupathy from the Thirumayam Assembly Constituency in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, after noting that the Election Petition was not filed by the election petitioner, but by his counsel.

“…an election petition is a serious proceeding which may result in the vitiation of an electoral process and that the procedure prescribed by an election statute must, therefore, be strictly followed.

The requirement that the petition be presented “by” the petitioner enables the High Court, at the stage of presentation itself, to undertake a preliminary verification so as to ensure that the proceeding is not frivolous or vexatious.”, the Court observed, relying on its 2009 judgment of G.V. Sreerama Reddy and Another.
Returning Officer and Others.
The petitioner, V. Pon.

Paneerselvam, who was a candidate on the Thirumayam seat, had challenged the election on allegations including corrupt practice of undue influence arising from alleged suppression and false declaration of his spouse's assets and income in the statutory Form 26 affidavit.
The Madras High Court dismissed the election petition, after finding that it had been presented by the petitioner's counsel rather than by the petitioner personally.
The petitioner approached the Supreme Court against the dismissal.

Refusing to interfere with the impugned findings, the judgment authored by Justice Mishra examined Sections 81 and 86 of the RP Act, which respectively prescribe the requirements for presentation of an election petition and the consequence of non-compliance.
Relying on its earlier decision in G.V. Sreerama Reddy.

Returning Officer, the Court noted that Section 81(1) contains five specific requirements: the petitioner must be a candidate or elector; the petition must be presented “by” the petitioner; it must be based on specified statutory grounds; it must be presented before the High Court; and it must be filed within the prescribed 45-day period.

stories.headline: MEA condemns Black Sea attacks on commercial shipping, says India engaging Russia and Ukraine to bring peace
stories.title: MEA condemns Black Sea attacks on commercial shipping, says India engaging Russia and Ukraine to bring peace
stories.summary: New Delhi [India], October 7 : Strongly condemning a series of recent attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea that put several Indian crew members at risk, India called for an immediate halt to maritime targeting and renewed its push for diplomatic mediation to end the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict. Addressing a bi-weekly press conference, Ministry of External Affairs Official Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal outlined an alarming surge in maritime safety threats, detailing four separate incidents involving merchant vessels operating in the region over 48 hours. Highlighting the immediate peril faced by merchant crews, Jaiswal noted that three Indian nationals were on board the commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov when it was struck, though they were safely rescued, while one injured person is receiving treatment. "We have seen a string of attacks in the Black Sea region in the last one or two days. We condemn such attacks that threaten commercial shipping and endanger the lives of our seafaring community. First, the commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov came under attack while it was plying in the Black Sea. There were three Indian nationals on board. All of them are safe, but one of them got injured and he's receiving medical treatment," Jaiswal stated. He said that the situation remained equally critical for other merchant vessels: the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan came under attack with the fate of its crew still unaccounted for, while the Palau-flagged MV ABLE was targeted by a drone strike. The Spokesperson further highlighted the rescue of an all-Indian crew following a strike on a Liberian-flagged oil tanker, Aframax Rio, where all 23 Indian seafarers on board were safely evacuated. "The second ship that came under attack was Alfa Watan. This is a Togo-flagged ship. It came under attack yesterday and the fate of its crew is unknown at this point. Another vessel, the Palau-flagged MV ABLE, came under a drone attack, but fortunately all 18 crew members, which includes seven Indian nationals, have been rescued. One Indian has been injured and is receiving medical assistance and supervision... The fourth ship, as I said earlier, came under attack. This is a Liberian-flagged oil tanker, Aframax Rio. All the crew members are Indian nationals—all 23 crew members on board this particular ship were Indian nationals—and all of them have been rescued," he added. Expanding on India's broader diplomatic efforts to address the root cause of regional volatility, the Ministry of External Affairs emphasised New Delhi's ongoing communication channels with both Moscow and Kyiv. Jaiswal reinforced India's long-standing position that sustainable solutions cannot be achieved on the battlefield, noting that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has repeatedly advocated for replacing prolonged military hostility with active conflict resolution. "On the issue, India has consistently maintained that dialogue and diplomacy are the way forward. We are aware of our position. Prime Minister on multiple occasions has expressed that the time has come for 'endless war to give way to an end to war'. In keeping with this idea to bring peace, India has engaged both sides, that is Russia and Ukraine. This has been appreciated by both Russia and Ukraine," Jaiswal explained. Detailing the practical scope of these diplomatic engagements, the Spokesperson stressed that India is actively working with both nations to secure critical supply lines, protect maritime trade routes, and mitigate global economic impacts. "We are trying to be helpful; India is trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, addressing immediate concerns of Russia and Ukraine on grain and energy exports and non-attack possibilities," Jaiswal concluded. "We have ongoing conversations with both Russia and Ukraine on this particular matter." Commercial maritime traffic across the Black Sea has faced escalating assaults since the onset of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in 2022, with both governments repeatedly targeting ships and marine infrastructure. Over recent days, Moscow has struck grain carriers transporting Ukrainian agricultural products close to Romania, an EU member state. Conversely, Kyiv maintains that its targeting of Russian petroleum infrastructure constitutes a legitimate response to nightly aerial bombardments hitting Ukrainian urban centres. Both belligerents have pledged to intensify their military operations in recent weeks, heightening anxieties regarding maritime security for commercial vessels navigating the Black Sea. Meanwhile, India has also stepped beyond traditional advocacy to actively broker peace and operational agreements between Moscow and Kyiv. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha confirmed that India has formally stepped forward to help resolve the conflict, offering what Kyiv considers "the most comprehensive" peace proposal currently under evaluation. Speaking at a press briefing, Sybiha disclosed that Kyiv is reviewing four distinct international proposals—including submissions from Turkey, Egypt, and the United States. Similarly, Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's efforts to bring an end to the conflict, noting that the Indian leader has "good ideas" for a peaceful resolution. (ANI)

stories.headline: RBI Rate Hike Explained: Higher EMIs, Costlier Loans? What It Means For Your Money
stories.title: RBI Rate Hike Explained: Higher EMIs, Costlier Loans? What It Means For Your Money
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has raised interest rates after 45 months, as rising prices, global uncertainties and the continuing Iran war add to economic risks. For consumers, the rate hike could mean higher borrowing costs across home, auto and personal loans, even as deposit rates may also rise gradually. A ₹50 lakh home loan for 20 years at 7.5% currently carries an EMI of around ₹40,280; a 25 basis point increase could push this to about ₹41,047. At the same time, the RBI has raised its GDP growth forecast for the current financial year to 7.1% from 6.7%, keeping India on track as the world’s fastest-growing major economy. But the message for India Inc. is mixed, with higher borrowing costs potentially affecting private capex and investment plans even as domestic growth remains strong. This is what the RBI’s latest move means for consumers, borrowers, savers and businesses.

article_sentences: The confirmation follows an August controversy, when 165 outgoing students, 409 students from other batches and 128 alumni opposed CJI Surya Kant's proposed convocation participation.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant will preside over the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru’s convocation ceremony for the outgoing batch on October 17, the university has confirmed.
The CJI will attend the event as NLSIU Chancellor, while theatre artist Arundhati Nag will be the Chief Guest and deliver the convocation address.
The confirmation comes weeks after a controversy over the proposed participation of the CJI at the university’s convocation.
In August, around 165 students from the outgoing 2026 batch, along with 409 students from other batches and 128 alumni, had opposed CJI Surya Kant being invited as the Chief Guest.

The protest came amid a similar boycott campaign at NALSAR University of Law, where students had opposed the CJI’s participation in its convocation over his comments concerning unemployed youngsters and student protests.
NLSIU students had also objected to the proposed attendance of Bar Council of India Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra at their ceremony.
Against this backdrop, NLSIU announced on August 27 that it was cancelling the convocation, citing “unavoidable circumstances”.
The university, however, revoked its decision last month and decided to proceed with the ceremony, without initially providing explicit confirmation on whether the CJI would attend.
The latest communication settles that uncertainty, confirming Surya Kant’s presence in his capacity as Chancellor.

With Arundhati Nag set to deliver the address, the October 17 ceremony will now bring together the university’s graduating students, faculty and guests following weeks of uncertainty surrounding the event.

stories.headline: Anup & Anup: The new chiefs facing execution tests at HDFC, Kotak
stories.title: Anup & Anup: The new chiefs facing execution tests at HDFC, Kotak
stories.summary: In a rare twist of timing, two bankers called Anup have been handed the keys to two of India's large private lenders. The appointments of Anup Bagchi at HDFC Bank and Anup Saha at Kotak Mahindra Bank (both as MD and CEO) on October 1 offers more than a curious symmetry. For two banking heavyweights, the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) approvals have simultaneously removed succession risk, allowing investors to refocus on growth, profitability and execution.By settling leadership questions at the top, the two private banks have not only eased a key overhang on valuations, but have also given investors greater confidence in the continuity of strategy, governance and execution.“The resolution of HDFC Bank and Kotak Mahindra’s management overhang within a week could mark a much-needed reset with historically attractive valuations, strong credit growth and potential FCNR-led liquidity/rate-cycle margin tailwinds supporting a broader re-rating,” says Anand Dama, Nuvama Institutional Equities. In August, banks had cumulatively raised $127.2 billion through RBI's FCNR(B) special window, which allowed foreign currency non-resident (bank) deposits.Also Read: What HDFC Bank chairman’s exit reveals about independent directors in IndiaYet, the journeys of both the Anups to the corner office could not be more different. Bagchi becomes the first outsider to run HDFC Bank, breaking with the lender's tradition of home-grown leaders. Saha, meanwhile, had joined Kotak Mahindra Bank (KMB) earlier this year. Although their routes have been different, they now face the same challenge: Shifting the market's attention from who runs the bank to how fast it can grow.Bagchi will take charge on October 27, succeeding Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose term ends a day earlier. Bagchi brings in over three decades of experience across banking, capital markets, wealth management and insurance. He has been associated with the ICICI Group since 1992 and has held leadership positions in ICICI Bank, ICICI Prudential Life and ICICI Securities. “An external appointment could provide HDFC Bank with a longer leadership runway and a cleaner slate to reassess its strategy, challenge existing practices and drive a strategic reset,” analysts at Nomura say.Saha, meanwhile, will take charge on January 1, succeeding Ashok Vaswani. Saha has been executive director at KMB, overseeing retail banking, government business, data analytics and marketing functions. He has over 32 years of professional experience, including 25 years in financial services across banking and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Before joining Kotak, he held a series of senior leadership roles at Bajaj Finance. Earlier, during 14 years at ICICI Bank, he led businesses and functions spanning retail secured assets, business intelligence, retail and rural collections, credit cards and retail structured finance.Both Anups have been handed full three-year terms, giving them the runway to execute on their strategic priorities. “The appointment of credible bankers could ease the protracted overhang on the stocks. Importantly, we believe the clarity around MD and CEO succession in the two heavyweights is also potentially a re-rating event for the sector,” says Jai Prakash Mundhra, analyst, ICICI Securities.Large private-sector banks have spent much of the past few years battling a series of overhangs, including leadership transitions at HDFC Bank and KMB, the HDFC Ltd integration, and RBI's digital/card restrictions to IndusInd Bank's derivatives accounting lapse.Also Read: Crack at the Top: What do top-level exits at banks indicate?The next battle: ExecutionBagchi takes charge of HDFC Bank as it experiences some of its toughest post-merger challenges, including shoring up deposits, accelerating loan growth and rebuilding margins. Analysts at Nomura feel his prior experience in building businesses and driving profitable growth could be relevant in addressing those priorities, while providing a fresh perspective on HDFC Bank’s operating framework.“The appointment removes succession uncertainty, with the focus now shifting to Bagchi’s strategic priorities and execution roadmap,” they say. While the external appointment provides an opportunity for a strategic reset, the pace of execution and clarity on the medium-term growth strategy will be critical for investor confidence and a sustained re-rating. Analysts will be watching Bagchi’s strategies on deposit mobilisation, sustaining loan growth, margin recovery and improvement in return ratios.Dama views Bagchi’s appointment as a long-term positive for the bank, given the strong leadership track record of ICICI bankers across the BFSI sector. “However, blending the distinct ICICI and HDFC Bank organisational DNA could pose near-term challenges with potential management rejig across businesses/subsidiaries. Thus, rebuilding the leadership team, sustaining growth, bolstering governance and restoring stakeholder confidence would be key priorities,” he explains.Apart from the merger-induced balance sheet issues and dip in competitiveness/profitability, HDFC Bank has navigated several challenges that have punctured investor confidence in the lender. Governance concerns deepened after the AT1 bond mis-selling controversy was followed by a rapid churn in the top leadership, including the unexpected exits of the chairman, MD and CEO, and several senior executives.In August, Jagdishan’s surprise decision to not seek reappointment as MD and CEO of HDFC Bank stunned investors. In March, its Chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned abruptly, citing differences over values and ethics. Rajiv Kumar, former chief election commissioner and former finance secretary, recently took charge as the new chairman after Chakraborty’s exit.In June, Bhavin Lakhpatwala, head of strategy and IR of HDFC Bank, resigned and joined RBL Bank as CFO. Puneet Sharma, former Axis Bank CFO, took charge as CFO-designate of HDFC Bank in September. The private lender’s current CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan is due to retire on November 30. Two of its long-standing directors, Sandeep Parekh and D Ranganathan, both members of the nominations and remuneration committee, will also reach their term limits in January 2027.In the last few months, HDFC saw a series of operational and governance issues. These include the marketing of Credit Suisse AT1 bonds, Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) deposits, the ensuing US class-action lawsuit, and mis-selling of Carlisle's Luxembourg Life Fund through its Dubai operations in 2019. Separately, the MSRDC deposit issue led the board to penalise Jagdishan, the CFO and retail assets head for ‘business overreach’.Given the change in leadership, Dama feels there could be another wave of management attrition across businesses and subsidiaries.Agrees Nitin Aggarwal, analyst, Motilal Oswal Financial Services. He also feels that a new leadership team, alongside an improvement in growth and earnings trajectory, should improve investor sentiment. Aggarwal estimates HDFC Bank to deliver an improved earnings performance from FY28 onward, while return-on-assets (RoA) may sustain at 1.7 percent (factoring in the potential cut in insurance commissions).For KMB as well, the key question now is what Saha's leadership means for strategy, as his appointment raises expectations of a stronger retail focus. Analysts at 360One Capital will be closely watching the bank's strategic direction, particularly in retail banking, given Saha’s extensive experience in consumer finance and retail banking at ICICI Bank and Bajaj Finance. His experience across retail banking, consumer finance, digital platform, analytics and operations would provide a broad leadership base for KMB’s focus on deepening customer relationships and driving sustainable growth.While execution remains a key for Saha as he takes charge at KMB, Gaurav Jani, analyst, Prabhudas Lilladher lists out issues that may need consideration. First is better loan growth than the current run rate of 14-16 percent given high capital adequacy. Second is strategy on gold loans, as KMB’s market share is not meaningful. Third is plan for the unsecured segment since gold credit is cannibalising unsecured loans.Also Read: Top leader leaves, then what? Corporate India’s succession challenge continuesHDFC Bank: Cleaning the deckHDFC Bank is undergoing management transition after a series of adverse developments, challenges in operating performance after its merger with HDFC and significant erosion of shareholder wealth over recent years. The changes in leadership are expected to address the scepticism around its growth.The share price of HDFC Bank has significantly underperformed peers over the last few years, with a tough adjustment period after the merger, and recent concerns about governance after Chakraborty’s exit, among other issues. The stock price has declined by 25 percent in the past year and 8 percent in the past five years.HDFC Bank has a formidable retail franchise, but its casa (current account saving account) ratio has come under pressure after the merger (32.3 percent as of June 2026). “Bagchi's experience in retail liabilities, digital channels, partnerships and third-party distribution would help improve customer acquisition and deepen existing relationships,” says Aggarwal. He also expects that Bagchi's experience could potentially help accelerate cross-selling across the bank’s large customer base and improve customer-level economics. The merger substantially enhanced HDFC Bank's mortgage and customer franchise but the bank has yet to fully demonstrate the operating leverage and cross-selling benefits that investors had initially expected.According to Mundhra, HDFC Bank needs to regain its low-cost funding edge, revive retail leadership and sharpen focus on select segments (self-employed, mid-corporate, gold loans, affordable, group synergies) while sustaining superior asset quality and management cohesiveness. He adds that the challenge for the new MD and CEO extends beyond preserving its strengths. It will require retaining key talent, building capabilities in strategic areas and establishing clearer accountability across the organisation to drive the next phase of growth. Equally important will be rebuilding investor confidence through a clear articulation of growth and profitability objectives, backed by well-defined priorities and execution timelines.Anup and Anup: The bankersBagchi brings more than three decades of experience across banking, capital markets and insurance. A career ICICI Group executive, he joined the group in 1992 and has held leadership roles across its banking and financial-services businesses.He served as MD & CEO of ICICI Securities between 2011 and 2016, overseeing the broking, wealth management and investment banking businesses. He later spent six years as executive director at ICICI Bank, leading retail banking, rural banking and digital channels. Since 2023, he has been MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.An engineer from IIT Kanpur and an MBA from IIM Bangalore, Bagchi brings experience in building retail franchises, driving digital adoption and managing large customer-facing businesses.Saha also brings more than three decades of experience across banking and financial services, with a strong focus on retail and MSME lending. Before joining KMB in January 2026, he spent over eight years at Bajaj Finance, where he held leadership roles across consumer finance, MSME lending, marketing, operations and digital platforms, culminating in his appointment as MD and CEO.Earlier, Saha spent 14 years at ICICI Bank, leading businesses spanning retail assets, credit cards, collections, business intelligence and structured finance. He has also worked with GE Capital and BHEL. A BTech graduate from IIT Kharagpur and an MBA from IIM Lucknow, Saha brings deep expertise in retail banking, consumer finance and scaled distribution businesses as he takes charge of KMB.

stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses To Interfere With Interim Bail To Congress Nandigram Candidate Milan Pradhan

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday upheld the interim bail granted to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who is contesting the Nandigram Assembly by-election, observing that the purpose of the relief was to enable him to contest the election and participate in the counting of votes.
Pradhan was arrested on 18th September, 2026 in criminal cases dating back 19 years arising from the 2007 Nandigram agitation.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana dismissed the West Bengal government's plea challenging the High Court's September 29 order granting Pradhan interim bail till October 21.
Voting for the by-election took place on October 6, while counting is scheduled for October 9.

The Court noted that although the cases registered against Pradhan include allegations of serious offences, the High Court's order was primarily intended to ensure that he was not denied an opportunity to contest the election.
The Court thus held that there was no need to interfere with the interim bail, which is operative till October 20, with Pradhan directed to surrender on October 21.
The State, however, will be entitled to raise all its contentions if Pradhan subsequently seeks an extension of interim bail or regular bail, the Court clarified.
“In such circumstances, we do not deem it necessary to interfere with the impugned order.

However, in case the respondent applies for extension of interim bail or seeks enlargement on regular bail, all the contentions raised before us shall be available to the State and shall be considered by the High Court in accordance with law,” the Court ordered.
The Court also made clear that it had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
During the hearing, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta sought to address the concern that Pradhan may have been arrested only because he was contesting the election.
Mehta took the Court through the allegations contained in the criminal cases pending against Pradhan.

stories.title: 'What Is This Scant Attitude To Court?' : Supreme Court Rebukes Centre For Non-Compliance On Welfare Of Disabled Military Cadets
stories.summary: The Court pulled up the Centre for not complying with its order to freshly consider the recommendations to grant Ex-Serviceman status and disability pension to such boarded out cadets.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday strongly criticised the Union government for failing to comply with its earlier directions to reconsider welfare measures for officer cadets boarded out of military training due to injuries or disabilities.
A bench of Justice BV Nagarathna, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice DK Upadhyaya was hearing the suo motu case concerning the plight of such cadets.

The Court expressed sharp dissatisfaction over the Centre's affidavit, noting that there had been no genuine reconsideration of the recommendations of the 2015 Sabharwal Committee report despite clear directions issued on August 4, 2026.
“What is this scant attitude you are showing to the court?
You say we disposed it of in 2022 and there ends the matter.
What is the attitude on the part of the department?” Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.

The bench pointed out that the Centre's affidavit merely referred to meetings held in 2022 and extracted earlier decisions rejecting disability pension and ex-servicemen (ESM) status for outboarded officer cadets.
There was “no whisper” that the Sabharwal Committee recommendations had been reconsidered in light of the court's intervention, the judges said.
Justice Mahadevan noted that one of the key recommendations relating to disability pension had not been revisited after the August 4 order.
“Pursuant to our 4th August direction, there is no reconsideration,” he said.

The Court observed that ordinary recruits who are boarded out receive disability pension and other benefits, while officer cadets - whose numbers are relatively small (around 400 over many years, or roughly 40 per year) - are denied similar treatment.
Amicus Curiae Senior Advocate Rekha Palli highlighted this disparity and submitted that the cadets were seeking parity.

stories.title: India, Canada hold NSA-level security dialogue, vow to combat transnational organised crime and terrorism
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 7: At the invitation of National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, the Senior Diplomatic and International Affairs Advisor to the Prime Minister of Canada, David Morrison visited India from 05-07 October 2026. MEA in a statement said, the meeting in New Delhi was held as part of the ongoing bilateral security dialogue at the NSA level. The previous dialogues in this format took place in New Delhi in September 2025 and in Ottawa in February 2026. It said that both sides acknowledged the guidance provided by their respective Prime Ministers during their meetings in New Delhi in March 2026 and on the margins of the G7 Summit in Évian in June 2026. The leaders noted with satisfaction the sustained and constructive bilateral engagements over the past year, guided by mutual trust, respect for each other’s concerns and sensitivities, and a shared commitment to strengthening bilateral relations. They welcomed efforts to advance negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). They also discussed the growing potential for advancing a substantive bilateral defence relationship in keeping with the vision of the leadership. During the meeting the two sides reviewed progress in bilateral security and law enforcement cooperation, including the implementation of the shared Security Work Plan concluded in February 2026. The two sides agreed to deepen coordination and cooperation in combating transnational organised crime, terrorism and violent extremism, human and drug trafficking, cybercrime, extortion, and extradition of criminal offenders. They also reaffirmed their commitment to identifying additional areas for practical cooperation, including exploring the establishment of structured dialogues on cyber security and economic security. Both sides agreed to strengthen existing institutional mechanisms and establish new channels, as appropriate, to facilitate streamlined communication and timely information-sharing on matters of mutual concern. The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments, MEA statement added.

stories.headline: Special NIA court rejects bail plea of separatist leader Shabir Shah in 1996 violence case
stories.title: Special NIA court rejects bail plea of separatist leader Shabir Shah in 1996 violence case
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 7: A special NIA court here has rejected the bail application of separatist leader Shabir Ahmad Shah in connection with a case arising from a 1996 FIR relating to violence, stone-pelting and firing on police personnel during a funeral procession in Srinagar. While rejecting the bail plea, Special Judge Prem Sagar held that the application "needs no consideration at this stage", observing that there was a "well-founded apprehension" that if released, Shah was likely to continue such activities to the detriment of national security and public order. Shah (73) was arrested in April by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in connection with the three-decade-old terror case related to mob violence and firing on policemen during a militant's funeral at Naaz crossing in Srinagar. His arrest came shortly after he was released on bail after nearly seven years of imprisonment in other NIA cases including one related to terror funding. Hearing the bail plea on Tuesday, the NIA court said it has already declared four persons as protected witnesses in the case and charges are yet to be framed against the accused. "Court is conscious of the fact that the only offence under the UAPA that is invoked against the applicant/accused is Section 13 only, which falls within Chapter III of the Act which does not attract the rigours of its Section 43-D(5) and the embargo on bail contained in Section 43-D(5) applies, by its express terms, only to offences 'punishable under Chapters IV and VI' of the Act but every case under UAPA has serious consequences and to be examined viz a viz nature of allegations, centrality of the role, protected witnesses, risk of intimidation, possibility of reactivation of networks etc," the judge said in his 23-page order. The order said any enlargement of the applicant on bail at this stage carries a reasonable apprehension of prejudice to the fair conduct of the trial and may adversely affect the confidence and security of the protected witnesses. On the plea of parity, the court ruled that Shah could not claim bail merely because some co-accused had been released. It distinguished their cases, noting that they had been granted bail after the investigation concerning them was over and the investigating officer no longer required their custody. The NIA had opposed the bail, arguing that Shah was allegedly a "principal leader of the procession", with the prosecution attributing to him an active role in allegedly raising provocative slogans and delivering inflammatory speeches before violence erupted. The agency also cited the presence of protected witnesses and apprehension of their intimidation. The NIA took over the investigation of the 1996 case in April on the directions of the Ministry of Home Affairs and subsequently filed a charge sheet before the NIA Special Court in Jammu on July 10. Shah along with other separatist leaders including Shakeel Ahmad Bakshi and Javid Ahmad Mir have been named in the charge sheet as accused in the case. Separatist leaders Syed Ali Shah Geelani, Abdul Gani Lone and Mohammad Yaqoob Wakeel were also named as accused, but proceedings against them abated following their death. Shah's counsel argued that the sole basis for rejection of his earlier bail plea as "premature" had ceased to exist, as the NIA had subsequently filed its charge sheet on July 10, and the investigation qua the applicant stood concluded. Counsel submitted that the earlier bail plea had not been rejected on merits and that, with the chargesheet now on record, there was no impediment to considering the plea on its merits. The defence also questioned the prosecution case, arguing that there was no allegation that Shah carried or used a weapon or fired any shot, with the firing attributed to unidentified armed persons. The defence also relied on Shah's prolonged incarceration, advanced age and the Supreme Court's March order granting him bail in another NIA case, arguing that continued detention would offend his right to speedy trial under Article 21.

stories.headline: Airtel hikes postpaid tariffs after over two years, sets the tone for peers
stories.title: Airtel hikes postpaid tariffs after over two years, sets the tone for peers
stories.summary: Airtel’s move comes just weeks ahead of the expected initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the parent of Reliance Jio, the market leader by subscribers.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India’s telecom tariff battle is back in play after an over two-year lull in postpaid charge revisions.
Bharti Airtel Ltd has raised prices across postpaid plans by 3-11%, a move that could possibly trigger a fresh round of industry-wide hikes in the chase for higher user spends.

Bharti Airtel, India’s second largest telecom operator by market share, has increased its tariffs by ₹50 across all its postpaid plans, also introducing its added benefit of free international roaming, Fast Lane technology, safety features and entertainment, the company said in a release on Wednesday.
The new tariffs will kick in on 8 October.
Airtel’s move comes just weeks ahead of the expected initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the parent of Reliance Jio, the market leader by subscribers.
A tariff increase can lift Airtel's revenues—and, in turn, valuations—putting pressure on Jio to follow suit as it prepares to sell shares to public investors.
For India's telecom industry, hiking tariffs and pushing subscribers up the value chain is the only way to bump up their revenues.
Airtel had last raised its headline tariffs in June 2024, after a gap of two years, following Jio.
The same was driven by the industry’s move to improve return on capital employed and Arpu.
Airtel's postpaid hikes in 2024 were in the 13-20% range.
That year, the tariff hikes were led by Jio, and its private sector peers Airtel and Vodafone Idea took cue.
Airtel currently has six postpaid plans.

stories.headline: CJI agrees to take a call on hearing a plea to recall split verdict in CEC appointments law case
stories.title: CJI agrees to take a call on hearing a plea to recall split verdict in CEC appointments law case
stories.summary: The application, filed by Naman Sherstra, was mentioned the previous week before Justice Dipankar Datta, who was the lead judge on the Bench which gave the split verdict
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine and take a call on hearing an application seeking a recall of a split verdict pronounced on September 23 in a case challenging the Election Commissioners’ appointments law.

The application, orally mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, questions why one of the judges on the apex court Bench, Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, did not reveal during multiple court proceedings that his son was a standing counsel for the Election Commission of India (ECI).
The application, filed by Naman Sherstra, was mentioned the previous week before Justice Dipankar Datta, who was the lead judge on the Bench which gave the split verdict.
Justice Datta had asked Sankaranarayanan to mention the application before the Chief Justice as the records of the case had already been returned to the CJI.

Sherstra has sought a recall of the opinion given by Justice Sharma, who was the puisne judge on the Division Bench headed by Justice Datta, on September 23 on the question of referring the challenge to the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 to a five-judge Bench.
While Justice Datta, in his opinion, had declined the reference to a Constitution Bench, Justice Sharma took an opposing view in favour of the reference.
Eventually, both judges on the Bench had passed a common order for the Chief Justice of India to allocate the case to a Constitution Bench.
The application has objected to this common order, but did not challenge, specifically, the separate opinion given by Justice Datta.

Justice Datta had observed in his opinion that 2023 law was prima facie wrong to ignore an earlier Constitution Bench judgment in the Anoop Baranwal case, which had included the Chief Justice of India as a neutral member in the Prime Minister-led selection panel for Chief Election Commissioners (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs).
The 2023 law had replaced the CJI with a Union Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
Justice Datta had said the replacement gave the Executive veto power over CEC/EC appointments, and reduced the presence of the Opposition Leader of the Lok Sabha to an ornamental status in the panel.
Justice Datta had reminded that the appointment and functioning of Election Commissioners was integral to free and fair elections.
